speaker: Unknown
en: Next up, we are honored to have Gabe with us.
zh: 接下来，我们很荣幸邀请到了 Gabe。

speaker: Unknown
en: Gabe is co-founder and president of Harvey.
zh: Gabe 是 Harvey 的联合创始人兼总裁。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were a research scientist at DeepMind ages ago, and then at Meta, I think, before you showed your college roommate what GPT-3 could do, and this duo then became Harvey.
zh: 你很久以前在 DeepMind 做过研究科学家，然后我想是在 Meta，在你给你的大学室友展示了 GPT-3 能做什么之前，随后你们二人组创立了 Harvey。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're really excited to have you here.
zh: 我们非常高兴你能来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think everybody here in the audience is an application company thinking about how to start doing their own research, post-training their own models.
zh: 我想在座的每一位都是应用公司，都在思考如何开始做自己的研究、对自己的模型进行后训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: And create their own labs.
zh: 并创建自己的实验室。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think Harvey has really set the example here and we're really delighted to have you give a talk on how you guys built Harvey Labs.
zh: 所以我认为 Harvey 在这方面真正树立了榜样，我们非常高兴请你做一个关于你们如何构建 Harvey Labs 的演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the alternative title to this talk is Building a Research Lab on a Budget.
zh: 这个演讲的另一个标题是“在预算内构建研究实验室”。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's an unfair game competing with the Frontier Labs if you're an application layer company.
zh: 如果你是一家应用层公司，与前沿实验室竞争是一场不公平的游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are rich teams, there are poor teams, and then there's us in the application layer.
zh: 有富有的团队，有贫穷的团队，然后还有我们这些应用层的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Frontier Labs have more money, more talent, more compute, infrastructure, and data.
zh: 前沿实验室有更多的钱、更多的人才、更多的算力、基础设施和数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do you compete?
zh: 那么你如何竞争？

speaker: Unknown
en: By using the Frontier ecosystem.
zh: 通过利用前沿生态系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we started Harvey four years ago, most of these companies either didn't exist or were just getting started.
zh: 当我们四年前创立 Harvey 时，这些公司中的大多数要么还不存在，要么才刚刚起步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we either had to build everything ourselves, or in most cases, focus on something different, like building our GTM org and a great product.
zh: 所以我们要么必须自己构建一切，要么在大多数情况下，专注于不同的事情，比如构建我们的 GTM 组织和一个伟大的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: But today, using the Frontier ecosystem, I think you can compete with the Frontier Labs and build Frontier Intelligence.
zh: 但今天，利用前沿生态系统，我认为你可以与前沿实验室竞争，并构建前沿智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: This talk is going to be our high-level playbook for doing this.
zh: 这个演讲将是我们做这件事的高层级行动手册。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm going to talk about how we build benchmarks and training data, how we work with the NeoLabs to do post-training, and how we serve these models in production.
zh: 我将谈谈我们如何构建基准测试和训练数据，我们如何与 NeoLabs 合作进行后训练，以及我们如何在生产环境中部署这些模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: To start, you want to build a benchmark.
zh: 首先，你要构建一个基准测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you don't have a good benchmark, you can't train models.
zh: 如果你没有一个好的基准测试，你就无法训练模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you can't train models, you don't need to serve them in production.
zh: 如果你不能训练模型，你就不需要在生产环境中部署它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this year we released three of these data sets that we built.
zh: 所以今年我们发布了三个我们构建的数据集。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started by building Legal Agent Bench, which is a taxonomy of tasks that associates would do at a large law firm.
zh: 我们首先构建了 Legal Agent Bench，这是一个大型律师事务所初级律师所做任务的分类体系。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these cover multiple practice areas, and there are complex tasks like drafting complex fund formation documents, doing case law research, things like that.
zh: 这些涵盖了多个执业领域，包括复杂的任务，比如起草复杂的基金设立文件、进行判例法研究，诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: We followed this up by building a contracting data set.
zh: 我们随后构建了一个合同数据集。

speaker: Unknown
en: This allows us to teach agents to do negotiation like you would in an in-house department.
zh: 这使我们能够教会智能体像在法务部门那样进行谈判。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the one I'm most excited about that we recently released is a large diligence dataset.
zh: 然后是我们最近发布的、我最兴奋的一个，是一个大型尽调数据集。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is, I think, one of the largest RL environments that's been released.
zh: 我认为这是已发布的最大的 RL 环境之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: The largest data rooms here are 80 million tokens.
zh: 这里最大的数据室有 8000 万 tokens。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it lets us do research on long context, very complex tasks.
zh: 它让我们能够对长上下文、非常复杂的任务进行研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the most interesting thing about these datasets is how we built them.
zh: 我认为这些数据集最有趣的地方在于我们如何构建它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: One challenge we always had at Harvey for training models is we can't train on our customers' data.
zh: 我们在 Harvey 训练模型时一直面临的一个挑战是，我们不能在客户的数据上训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: We work with the largest law firms and enterprises, and their legal data is incredibly sensitive.
zh: 我们与最大的律师事务所和企业合作，他们的法律数据极其敏感。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's privileged.
zh: 这些数据受特权保护。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you can't put it in generic models.
zh: 所以你不能把它放进通用模型里。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can't even put it in our models.
zh: 我们甚至不能把它放进我们自己的模型里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so how do you train models given that?
zh: 那么在这种情况下，你如何训练模型？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the thing that started working really well this year is using domain experts to guide synthetic data generation.
zh: 而今年开始非常有效的方法，是使用领域专家来引导合成数据生成。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Brendan from our core had a good analogy that the same way that engineers now don't write code, they vibe code and guide these coding models, we're starting to do the same thing.
zh: 我们核心团队的 Brendan 有一个好的类比：就像现在的工程师不再写代码，而是 vibe code 并引导这些编码模型一样，我们也开始做同样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so my younger brother is actually a lawyer at Harvey and he's gotten very good at using the coding models.
zh: 我的弟弟实际上是 Harvey 的一名律师，他已经非常擅长使用这些编码模型了。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's trained our other lawyers to do that and they can generate incredibly realistic data sets that we can use for training and also evaluating our product.
zh: 他培训了我们其他的律师这么做，他们可以生成极其逼真的数据集，我们可以用于训练，也可以用于评估我们的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And once you've done that, synthetic data isn't good enough, but it's a way to get started.
zh: 而一旦你做到了这一点，合成数据还不够好，但它是一个入门的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we work with companies like Mercore and Snorkel who let you scale up this process and build larger sets, particularly for training.
zh: 所以我们与像 Mercore 和 Snorkel 这样的公司合作，它们让你可以扩大这一流程并构建更大的数据集，特别是用于训练的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once you've done that, you need to turn these data sets into efficient RL environments.
zh: 一旦你做到了这一点，你需要把这些数据集转化为高效的 RL 环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: It gets really expensive as these data sets get larger and evaluation gets very expensive.
zh: 随着这些数据集变大，成本会变得非常高，评估也变得非常昂贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, in our diligence data set, we have over a thousand unit tests that are grading model outputs using LLM as a judge.
zh: 例如，在我们的尽调数据集中，我们有超过一千个单元测试，使用 LLM 作为裁判来给模型输出打分。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you use the largest models and you want to do RL rollouts and things like this, it gets very expensive.
zh: 如果你使用最大的模型，并且你想做 RL rollout 之类的事情，成本会变得非常高。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's a lot of work, and here's some we did with LangChain, of making these very efficient.
zh: 所以有很多工作，这里有一些是我们与 LangChain 一起做的，就是让这些变得非常高效。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the last thing we did that I think was a little controversial at the time was open sourcing some of these data sets.
zh: 然后我们做的最后一件事，我认为当时有些争议，就是将其中一些数据集开源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the motivation for this was it's very hard to know your data set is good unless a lot of people train on it.
zh: 这么做的动机是,除非有很多人在你的数据集上训练,否则很难知道你的数据集是不是好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I used to do research at Google Brain and DeepMind, the best data sets were open, like ImageNet, CIFAR, MNIST, and everyone used them.
zh: 我以前在 Google Brain 和 DeepMind 做研究的时候,最好的数据集都是开放的,比如 ImageNet、CIFAR、MNIST,所有人都用它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you were able to find all of the issues.
zh: 这样你就能发现所有的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we get a ton of pull requests.
zh: 我们收到了大量的 pull request。

speaker: Unknown
en: We get suggestions.
zh: 我们收到各种建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I think increasingly, we're having the labs, when they report new models, benchmark on our data set.
zh: 然后我觉得,越来越多的实验室在发布新模型时,会在我们的数据集上做基准测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then most importantly, we had Elon retweet it.
zh: 最重要的是,Elon 转发推文了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So once you've built the benchmark, now you have something to train models against.
zh: 所以一旦你构建了基准,现在你就有了可以用来对照训练模型的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the thing that is exciting now is open source models are getting competitive.
zh: 现在令人兴奋的是,开源模型正在变得有竞争力。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the past, it wasn't worth doing post-training because the models were improving so quickly from pre-training that any post-training you did quickly got absorbed by the next pre-trained model.
zh: 过去做后训练是不值得的,因为模型通过预训练提升得太快,你做的任何后训练很快就会被下一个预训练模型吸收掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now with models like Kimi3, GLM 5.2, Nemotron, Inkling, and others, it's possible to take these very strong open source-based models and post-train them to levels of frontier intelligence.
zh: 但现在,有了 Kimi3、GLM 5.2、Nemotron、Inkling 等等这样的模型,可以把这些非常强的开源基础模型做后训练,达到前沿智能的水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe not general frontier intelligence, but if you have a specific task like us,
zh: 也许不是通用的前沿智能,但如果你有一个具体的任务,比如像我们这样,

speaker: Unknown
en: They are competitive.
zh: 它们是有竞争力的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the way we recommend getting started is working with the NeoLabs.
zh: 所以我们推荐的入门方式是和 NeoLabs 合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have a bunch of expertise and infrastructure already in place to help you make sure that your training data sets are good.
zh: 他们已经有大量的专业知识和基础设施,可以帮助你确保你的训练数据集是好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have recipes.
zh: 他们有现成的配方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And usually, if you work with them and you're not able to get better results, there's probably something you're doing wrong with your data set.
zh: 通常,如果你和他们合作却没能得到更好的结果,那很可能是你的数据集有问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is a very good way to bootstrap it.
zh: 这是很好的起步方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so some of the interesting work we did with these different providers.
zh: 以下是我们和这些不同提供商所做的一些有趣的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fireworks, we got some very interesting results training GLM 5.1 to use Fable or maybe Opus 4.8 as an advisor model.
zh: Fireworks,我们得到了一些非常有趣的结果,训练 GLM 5.1 使用 Fable 或者也许是 Opus 4.8 作为顾问模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Base 10, we did some interesting work on KV compaction.
zh: Base 10,我们做了一些关于 KV 压缩的有趣工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Engram, who I think is here, we're doing interesting work on enterprise search and firm knowledge.
zh: Engram,我想他们的人在场,我们正在企业搜索和公司知识方面做有趣的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Trajectory, we worked with them to train Nemotron models.
zh: Trajectory,我们和他们合作训练 Nemotron 模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Applied Compute, we're doing some interesting work on our Vault product.
zh: Applied Compute,我们正在我们的 Vault 产品上做一些有趣的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think one question we got is, why work with multiple NEO labs?
zh: 我记得我们收到的一个问题是,为什么要和多个 NEO 实验室合作?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why not just pick one?
zh: 为什么不只挑一个?

speaker: Unknown
en: And for us, as we're scaling the research lab,
zh: 对我们来说,随着研究实验室的扩张,

speaker: Unknown
en: We have more research projects than we have bandwidth to do internally or just with a single Neolab.
zh: 我们的研究项目比我们内部、或者只和单个 Neolab 合作所能承受的带宽要多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And every Neolab is taking a different bet.
zh: 而且,每个 Neolab 押注的方向都不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have different ways they think about research.
zh: 他们看待研究的方式各不相同。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have different open source models we want to train.
zh: 我们想要训练的开源模型也不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the more we work with, the more we learn.
zh: 我们合作的越多,学到的就越多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's getting easier than ever to do post-training.
zh: 而且现在做后训练比以往任何时候都容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one, working with the NeoLabs, we're learning a lot in partnership with them.
zh: 第一,和 NeoLabs 合作,我们在合作中学到了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we're doing more and more post-training ourselves internally with APIs like Tinkerer and the infrastructure of Fireworks and Base 10 have built.
zh: 然后我们自己在内部也越来越多地做后训练,使用像 Tinkerer 这样的 API,以及 Fireworks 和 Base 10 构建的基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's never been easier to post-train these models and then serve them.
zh: 对这些模型做后训练然后把它们部署上线,从来没有这么容易过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's increasingly more post-training talent that we're hiring and is available.
zh: 而且后训练人才越来越多,我们正在招聘,人才市场上也有。

speaker: Unknown
en: And inspired by Cursor, the goal of these efforts is for us to build our version of Composer 1.
zh: 受 Cursor 启发,这些努力的目标是为我们打造自己版本的 Composer 1。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we package all of the work we've done with synthetic data, scaling it with Mercor, the work with the NeoLabs into a model we can serve alongside the closed source models?
zh: 如何把我们用 Mercor 扩展合成数据的工作、和 NeoLabs 合作的工作,打包成一个可以和闭源模型一起部署的模型?

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, once you've post-trained a model, you need to be able to serve it in production.
zh: 现在,一旦你对模型做了后训练,你就需要能够在生产环境中部署它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is non-trivial.
zh: 而这不是一件小事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I want to start first by talking about our model-serving infrastructure because I think sometimes people still think about application layer companies as you're calling a single model endpoint and it's maybe a chat product.
zh: 所以我想先从我们的模型部署基础设施讲起,因为我觉得有时人们仍然认为应用层公司就是调用单个模型端点,可能是一个聊天产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a big problem we've solved over the past four years is we operate in 60 countries.
zh: 而我们在过去四年里解决的一个大问题是,我们在 60 个国家运营。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have multiple product surface areas.
zh: 我们有多个产品界面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Customers have different model preferences.
zh: 客户有不同的模型偏好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even with just the closed source models, how do you serve these at scale?
zh: 即使只有闭源模型,你如何大规模地部署它们?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this matrix gives you a sense of all of the things we need to handle when we're thinking about serving these models at scale.
zh: 这个矩阵可以让你了解,在考虑大规模部署这些模型时,我们需要处理的所有事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as a simple example, for each of these model families, we need to serve multiple of these models.
zh: 举个简单的例子,对于每一个模型家族,我们都需要部署多个模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to have fallbacks across providers to hit our SLAs.
zh: 我们需要在提供商之间设置备选方案,以达到我们的 SLA。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now with companies like Fireworks Base 10, we can add open source models into this mix.
zh: 现在,有了 Fireworks、Base 10 这样的公司,我们可以把开源模型加入到这个组合中。

speaker: Unknown
en: In order to think about when you serve models in production and how you monitor them in production, you need to have this infrastructure in place even before you think about post-training.
zh: 为了思考在生产环境中服务模型以及如何在生产环境中监控它们，你需要在考虑后训练之前就把这些基础设施准备好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is how we think about when there's a new model released, whether it's open source, closed source, or a model we've post-trained, how we make decisions whether to put it in production.
zh: 这就是我们思考的方式：当有新模型发布时，无论是开源的、闭源的，还是我们做过后训练的模型，我们如何决定是否将其投入生产。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then once it's in production, how we make decisions whether to keep it in production.
zh: 然后一旦投入生产，我们如何决定是否继续保留它在生产环境中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so pre-production we have a set of generic evals.
zh: 在投入生产之前，我们有一套通用的评测。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in terms of automated we have the lab benchmark that I talked about where whenever a new model comes out this gives us a very quick sense of is it a frontier model?
zh: 在自动化方面，我们有我之前提到的实验室基准，每当有新模型发布时，这能让我们很快判断它是不是一个前沿模型？

speaker: Unknown
en: How strong is it?
zh: 它有多强？

speaker: Unknown
en: What areas of legal is it good?
zh: 它在法律领域的哪些方面表现好？

speaker: Unknown
en: We have human testing in the generic case where we run side-by-sides of this model with other models to compare them.
zh: 在通用情况下，我们有人工测试，我们会把这个模型与其他模型进行并排对比。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then for every product surface we have critical user journeys and automated product tests because a model could be very good generically but it could not be a good fit for a specific product surface.
zh: 然后对于每个产品界面，我们有关键用户旅程和自动化产品测试，因为一个模型可能在整体上非常出色，但它可能不适合某个特定的产品界面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we also have human product testing.
zh: 然后我们还有人工产品测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And together these signals along with heuristics around cost, latency, region availability is how we decide whether we put a model into production.
zh: 这些信号加上围绕成本、延迟、区域可用性的启发式规则，就是我们决定是否将模型投入生产的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the important point here is
zh: 我认为这里重要的一点是

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the case for post-trained models or non-post-trained models.
zh: 这对做过后训练的模型或没做过后训练的模型都是适用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you can reuse this infrastructure, and you should have it in place before you think about post-training.
zh: 所以你可以复用这些基础设施，而且你应该在考虑后训练之前就把它准备好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once a model's in production, same thing, doesn't matter if the model's post-trained or not.
zh: 一旦模型投入生产，同样的事情，不管模型有没有做过后训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do A-B testing if we're rolling out a large change.
zh: 如果我们要推出一个大的变更，我们会做 A/B 测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: We look at engagement to track if this model's performing how we expect.
zh: 我们通过观察用户参与度来追踪这个模型是否按我们预期的方式运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we look at things like uptime token efficiency.
zh: 然后我们会看正常运行时间、token 效率之类的指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we call it product feedback.
zh: 然后我们称之为产品反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: I call it angry customer emails.
zh: 我称之为愤怒的客户邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's all of these signals that tell you this is working as expected.
zh: 所有这些信号都会告诉你，这一切是否按预期运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you need that infrastructure in place before you think about serving models.
zh: 所以你需要在考虑服务模型之前就准备好这些基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the thing you need to do even still before serving models is what I call the simple open source switches.
